feat(models): default z.ai GLM to glm-5.4 (#3644)

z.ai released GLM-5.4 on 2026-11-23 on its Coding Plan, the
/api/anthropic wire iterion reaches z.ai through. Every default that
names z.ai's GLM moves to it:

- secrets.ZAIDefaultModel ("glm-5.4") is the one Go source: detect's
  and the cloud catalogue's z.ai suggestion (the model a claw node with
  no model lands on when only z.ai is credentialed) read it.
- The catalogue's GLM rescue routes (review-pr reviewer_alternate,
  revi-converse converse_agent, gitops-warden classify) name glm-5.4;
  each manifest carries a patch bump. The Revi default-walk golden and
  map-bots follow.
- bots/catalog_zai_default_model_test.go holds every z.ai GLM route of
  the catalogue (node model, fallback, zai:<model> chain element) to
  ZAIDefaultModel, with a floor on how many routes it must see.
- `iterion models` lists anthropic/glm-5.4; the GLM window comment and
  the generation test pin 5.4 at 1M (models.dev:
  zai-coding-plan/glm-5.4, 1M ctx / 131072 out).
- Docs, the DSL quickref, sec-audit's chain example, the e2e narrowing
  fixture and the z.ai live probe move with it. Scaleway routes stay on
  glm-5.3: Scaleway does not serve 5.4 (no open weights yet).

glm-5.4 has no published price yet (models.dev lists it at 0 on the
coding plan only; OpenRouter does not serve it), so its tokens book as
unpriced spend: an advisory budget warning, never a refusal. The
known-zero extraction test seeds its price fixture from
ZAIDefaultModel instead of a literal 5.3.

Proof: ZAI_LIVE_PROBE=1 TestLiveZaiStream green on glm-5.4; a direct
/v1/messages call answers "model":"glm-5.4" (HTTP 200) while glm-9.9
is refused 400/1211, so z.ai does not alias an unknown id.
Mutated: gitops-warden's route back on 5.3, review-pr's route back on
5.3, the walk's fallback check removed (floor red), ZAIDefaultModel
back on 5.3 (detect_test red); each red on its own assertion, restored
byte-identical.

Refs #3631

Landed by admin bypass of the merge queue. revi/review and the
required set (test, race, vendor-check, mongo-conformance, golangci,
brand) were green on 8d81b90e. The queue ejected the PR twice, each
time on race-shard legs this diff does not reach:
internal/fswatch TestEveryRawWatcherAddGoesThroughFswatch (go list
-export killed at 600s), pkg/dsl/ir TestNodeChainCompilesLinearly
(11.3s against a 10s budget) and pkg/runview/runstream
TestFileSourceSettleWindowRechecksAResumedRun. The same legs were red
on main pushes in the same window, and the two latter tests are green
locally under -race (3/3, 10/10).
Integration train: origin/main 8f2068563 + 8d81b90e merged --no-ff
(ed4510ee7, clean): task -x fmt:check and task -x check exit 0;
go test -race green on pkg/backend/detect, pkg/backend/model,
pkg/modelcatalog, pkg/secrets, pkg/server/cloudpublisher,
internal/mdcode, cmd/iterion and the bots tests the diff changes (the
whole bots package under -race outruns go test's 600s default; CI
bounds it at 2400s and ran it green on the PR head). main did not move
between the train and this merge.

Gate-Bypass: merge queue ejected on race-shard flakes unrelated to the diff — #3644

feat(server): alarm the operator when a schedule stops producing successful runs (#3655)

* feat(server): alarm the operator when a schedule stops producing successful runs

A cloud schedule that stopped delivering reached nobody: its row carries its health (next_fire_at, last_error, last_run_status) but only pull surfaces read it, and the ops dispatcher sees runs, not ticks refused before any run or a scheduler that stopped claiming slots.

cloudsched.AssessScheduleStall evaluates the row (overdue > launch refused > failed/parked run, disabled and cancelled never alarm), each cause self-clearing with a stable episode id. Store.ListEnabled lists enabled schedules cross-tenant on both twins. A 10-minute sweep on every replica sends a new schedule_stalled alert through OpsDispatcher.NotifyOperator; the shared claim delivers one alert per episode. Tracker level: warning.

Mutated: grace comparison, cancelled-as-failed, precedence, refusal anchor, ListEnabled filter, per-sweep episode key, tracker level, title, run fields — each reddened its test.

Closes #3594

Mutation: Scripted bench ($TMPDIR/new-vigie-monitor/mut.py). For each mutation: replace the production line, run the targeted test, write back the original bytes, and assert that the sha256 matches the original. Every mutation went red on its own assertion. M1 watch.go `now.Sub(sb.NextFireAt) > grace` -> `now.After(sb.NextFireAt)`: TestAssessScheduleStall watch_test.go:65 'want healthy (nil)' on the due-within-grace row. M2 `status == store.RunStatusFailedResumable` -> `status.IsTerminalResumable()`: :65, the cancelled row alarms. M3 upstream precedence broken: :73 'cause = launch_refused, want overdue'. M4 LastErrorAt anchor disabled: TestAssessScheduleStallEpisodes :101 'refusal raised again after a clear reused episode'. M5 memory ListEnabled keeps disabled rows: TestMemoryStoreListEnabled :148. M6 server episode key minted per sweep (+time.Now().String()): TestScheduleOutcomeWatch :70 'two sweeps delivered 2 alerts, want 1' and ReplicasDeliverOnce :141 '4 alerts, want 1'. M7 errtrack drops KindScheduleStalled from the warning case: schedule_stalled_test.go:51 'tracker events = 0, want 1'. M8 Title case removed: :21 'Title() = Run alert: feed-watch'. M9 run fields set on every cause: schedule_outcome_watch_test.go:102 'refused launch must alert once, naming no run'. After the bench, git status showed only the intended files, and each file's hash matched its pre-mutation content.

Review fixes:
- AssessScheduleStall counts the overdue grace from the later of next_fire_at and updated_at. The episode key and the age shown in the reason still come from next_fire_at. The StallOverdue godoc and the docs/scheduling.md overdue bullet are updated to match.
- Ticker.fireIntent computes hold := ctx.Err()!=nil || errors.Is(lerr, ErrMaintenanceHold) once and passes it to finish(hold). It calls recordLaunchVerdict only when !hold. The audit record is unchanged, so it still carries the hold.
- Pins the schedule id in the episode claim key. The new test has two schedules refused in one real Ticker.Tick (org_suspended, not a hold) and expects 2 alerts. A second case has two rows overdue on the same next_fire_at and also expects 2 alerts.
- Documentation only, as the verifier prescribed. docs/scheduling.md now states that a schedule held by a live run under overlap: skip is not watched, that a live run with no activity raises the run-level stall alert and one waiting for a human is a decision, and that the symptom is last_fire_at moving while last_run_at stays put. No fourth cause was added.

Closes #3594

* fix(cloudsched): keep only the armed maintenance fence silent on the schedule watch

The ticker skipped the launch verdict on every ErrMaintenanceHold. When an unreadable fence record or a Mongo persistence failure lasted, nothing launched and no schedule_stalled alert fired. The armed fence now unwraps to the new schedgate.ErrMaintenanceFenceArmed, which still wraps ErrMaintenanceHold. launchDenial.fenceArmed is set on the armed denial only, and the ticker skips the verdict only for that sentinel. Other holds still keep the slot but write last_error. Each mutation went red on its own test and was restored byte-identical: ticker back to !hold, fenceArmed dropped, Unwrap ignoring FenceArmed, fenceArmed on the read-error denial, err() not copying it.

Follow-up of the closing review on #3594: a confirmed medium, fixed with its verified remedy; bounded closing round on this fix: no high or critical (5 lower findings, deferred).

ci: run race/e2e legs in the merge queue only and split pkg/server across race shards (#3688)

A pull request without the ci:full label skips race-shard, test-e2e and cloud-e2e. The merge queue and main still run them, so a change no longer pays the heavy suite twice (#3683). test and race read LIGHT_PULL_REQUEST, the negation of the legs' own condition as evaluated by GitHub, and accept a skipped heavy leg only when it is true. On merge_group and push a skipped heavy leg is red. ciguard pins the condition at every reader and runs each aggregator under both values.

race-shard no longer packs pkg/server whole. Each shard runs a test-name hash slice of it beside its packages (#3684), and a discovery failure turns the shard red. Its weights row is gone. Mutated: forgive clause, leg if:, env spelling, -skip, wait status, discovery assignment, weights row.



Mutation: Every mutation was made in production (tests.yml or the weights table), one at a time, and restored with cp from a backup. sha256sum -c of both files printed OK afterwards. M1: removed `&& [ "$LIGHT_PULL_REQUEST" = "true" ]` from test's forgive clause. TestAggregatorsGoRedOnEveryRedLeg went red: routing_test.go:591 'aggregator "test" stays GREEN when leg test-e2e reports skipped with LIGHT_PULL_REQUEST="false"'. M2: reverted the heavy legs' if: to the tap skip alone. TestEveryJobPicksASideOfTheMergeQueue went red: routing_test.go:363 'job "race-shard" is a heavy leg and carries `if:` ...'. M3: set LIGHT_PULL_REQUEST to `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`. TestAggregatorsReVerifyEveryLeg went red: routing_test.go:497. M4: took pkg/server out of race-shard's -skip. Red: race_server_split_test.go:81 'still packs pkg/server whole'. M5: changed `wait "$server_pid" || server_status=$?` to `|| true`. Red: race_server_split_test.go:175 'step green=true, want false' (server-slice-fails). M6: changed the discovery assignment to end with `|| true`. Red: race_server_split_test.go:167 'the step succeeded after pkg/server discovery failed'. M7: changed cloud-e2e's `&&` to `||`. Red: routing_test.go:378. M8: put the pkg/server row back in test-shards-weights.tsv. TestTheCommittedWeightsTablesPackTheirLegs went red: main_test.go:542 'row(s) match no package this leg packs'.

Review fixes:
- Raised the by-name test discovery bound from -list-timeout 5m to 10m on race-shard's pkg/server discovery and on test-e2e's ./e2e discovery. Discovery is still bounded, so a failure still turns the check red. The step comments now give the bound and say the run reuses the compile. merge-policy.md now says the default is five minutes and CI passes ten.
- A light PR's green test/race is now marked not admin-mergeable. Both aggregators' ::notice:: now says 'so this green is not admin-mergeable'. The parked-gate item 1 and the incident fast lane in merge-policy.md now require the `ci:full` label, a push after labelling, and every `race-shard (n)` and `test-e2e (n)` at `success`, not `skipped`, on the head. 'nothing else' is replaced: without ci:full the bypass also skips -race and e2e. The 'What this bypass gives up' paragraph now says the heavy legs run through ci:full. The light-PR section states the rule and links both lanes. Step 3 of review-and-merge.md now says 'under `ci:full` on a light pull request' and links the parked gate. It is kept short because of that page's 12288-byte budget.
- Corrected the 'floor of every race run' claim at all three sites (the tests.yml comment, merge-policy.md and the race_server_split_test.go godoc). pkg/server ran ~1434 s, the largest package after bots (~1630-1715 s). bots still runs whole and stays the floor of the race wall. #3684's ~20 min acceptance is not claimed.
- The ci:full guidance in merge-policy.md now names each opt-in job and when to use it: `race-shard` and `test-e2e` for concurrency, the engine or e2e, and `cloud-e2e` for a change to `charts/` or the cloud stack. The workflow condition is unchanged.
- The discovery-bound guard now matches any testshards call whose arguments carry -tests, in either the '-tests X' or the '-tests=X' spelling and in any flag order. It also accepts '-list-timeout=D'. It reads every .github/workflows/*.yml and *.yaml file, and fails on a glob error or when no workflow file is found. The per-call judgement moved into discoveryProblems(path, text) and the file list into discoveryWorkflows(t), so the regression test calls the same code the guard runs.

Closes #3683
